title: Evidence Archive Streams and Automated Certified Reports
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a tenant-aware export pipeline that produces verifiable compliance artifacts (PDF and CSV bundles) with configurable retention and residency enforcement. The feature will: generate signed PDF summaries and raw CSV slices for requested time windows; group evidence into per-tenant archives routed to the correct data residency region; support scheduled recurring exports and ad-hoc pulls; attach cryptographic hashes and a signed manifest for auditor verification; and provide delivery targets (S3, SFTP, email with signed links). Exports must honor tenant retention rules (auto-delete artifacts after retention period) and encryption keys (customer-managed KMS where enabled). The implementation must integrate with the Console dashboards to show export status, size, delivery latency, and last successful run, and expose audit logs for each export event.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create scheduled export jobs scoped to tenants, namespaces, and time ranges (daily/weekly/monthly) via Console UI and API
Exports produced in both PDF and CSV formats; PDFs contain human-readable certified summary with export metadata and signed manifest; CSVs contain raw event rows used by audits
Each export bundle includes a manifest.json and a PKCS7 or detached signature (SHA256) that auditors can validate
Export delivery honors tenant data residency: bundles for EU-resident tenants are stored/delivered from eu- region S3 or equivalent endpoints
Retention enforcement: export artifacts are auto-deleted according to tenant retention policy and appear in retention audit logs
Delivery options supported: S3 (presigned), SFTP push, and encrypted email link; failures retried with exponential backoff and visible in Console
Console dashboard widgets updated: export success rate, average time-to-deliver, total bytes exported, and per-tenant last-run timestamp
E2E integration tests and a security review are completed before GA; performance tests for up to 5TB/day export throughput documented
notes: Trade-off: generating PDFs server-side increases CPU usage and latency; consider offloading PDF rendering to a worker fleet with autoscaling
Decision: use a signed manifest with SHA256 digests and a service-level signing key; provide option to include tenant KMS signature for enterprise customers
Risk: delivering large archives over email/SFTP can hit client limits; recommend S3 presigned link as primary path for >100MB bundles
Telemetry: record token-level export cost, bytes per tenant, and time-in-queue metrics for runtime optimization
Consider adding incremental export mode that streams only changed records since last successful export to reduce bandwidth for large tenants
